title: Here's what's driving this week's $1 trillion wipeout in chip stocks
content:
The AI trade is taking it on the chin this week.
Investors dumped high-flying chip and memory stocks for a second day on Thursday, with the largest names in the sectors shedding more than $1 trillion in market cap this week.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down 12% from its peak in early October. The index is on track for its seventh day of losses, which would mark its worst losing streak since May 2025.
The major indexes shook off the volatility and pared their earlier losses in the afternoon. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained more than 500 points, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq was flat.
Here's where US indexes stood at the 4 p.m. ET closing bell:
- S&P 500: 7,744.06, up 0.33%
- Dow Jones Industrial Average: 52,177.69, up 1.08% (+556.21 points)
- Nasdaq 100: 29,935.59, down 0.5%
Here were some of the most notable moves in the chips and AI space:
Here are the factors behind the latest burst of selling across the chips space:
1. Spillover effects from South Korea
The sell-off appeared to begin in South Korea this week. It's a highly-leveraged market that's been rattled by extreme volatility numerous times this year already. SK Hynix and Samsung, which make up more than half of the market cap of the country's KOSPI stock index, began sliding on Tuesday as investors aired concerns about lofty valuations in the sector. The selling quickly spread into areas like Japan and the US.
Investors began selling chip stocks in earnest after Chinese chip firm CXMT said it made progress on a new, denser chip architecture, sparking fears China could be catching up to international memory chip makers.
2. Hot inflation
Hotter-than-expected inflation data has also dampened investor sentiment. September inflation grew at a 3.7% pace, slightly above the 3.6% expected. Producer prices also rose at a 6.3% annual pace in September, its fastest pace since 2022.
Markets are pricing in a 92% probability that the Fed will hike rates at least one more time through the end of the year.
"With a second day in a row of higher-than-expected inflation numbers, it seems the Fed will have no choice but to raise rates again this year," Chris Zaccarelli, the chief investment officer at Northlight Asset Management, said.
Investors flipped the script on the bond sell-off as stocks tumbled. The flight-to-safety trade was in full effect, with 10-year Treasury yield plummeting 13 basis points to 5.06%, even as red-hot inflation readings raised the odds of rate hikes from the Fed.
3. Higher borrowing costs
Higher-for-longer interest rates have been on investors' minds lately, with the recent spike in bond yields adding to the risk-off mood. The 10-year US Treasury yield rose as high as 5.34% in early October before pulling back to around the 5% mark on Thursday, remaining near multi-decade highs.
As yields rise, fears are growing that US Treasurys and hyperscaler debt will increasingly compete for investor capital, driving the yields up for both.
"The concern is that these will cut into future returns, even as the likely timing and size of these returns is far from clear," David Morrison, a senior market analyst at Trade Nation, wrote in a note.
4. Concerns about overspending, slowing revenue
Anthropic told investors it made $16.8 billion in revenue in the third quarter.
Bearish market watchers say the results mark a "worrisome deceleration" from the prior quarter's growth, when revenue more than doubled from $4.7 billion to $11.5 billion, DA Davidson said.
All this is once again raising concerns that tech giants may be overspending on artificial intelligence. The hyperscalers are on track to spend around $800 billion on capex this year, according to a Goldman Sachs report.
"The big story of last night, and really the reason for a tremendous amount of market angst in the last several sessions, was the anticipation and fear around Anthropic's updated #'s," analysts at Jefferies wrote in a client note.
Also on Thursday, CoreWeave stock plunged as investors eyed a spike in its bond yields. The neocloud company has seen its bonds due in 2032 surge from 9.625% when they were issued in June, to almost 15% this week.
Morrison flagged the worry among some investors that tech giants may be "overspending on capacity which may never get used."
Some analysts are eyeing the possibility that the chips rout may be nearing its end. Strategists on JPMorgan's market intelligence team floated a possible "inflection point" in the sector, given how chip stocks remain around 15% below their all-time highs in June.
"We think Semis can climb this latest wall of worry as recent earnings updates from Hynix / Samsung point to on-going thematic strength. Separately, breadth continues to deteriorate which we think can reverse into / out of earnings season which will buttress the rally," the bank wrote earlier this week.

report.summary: AI芯片股一周蒸发超1万亿美元，估值、通胀与支出担忧共振
report.background: 2024年以来，AI算力投资热潮推动英伟达、SK海力士、三星等芯片与存储股持续走高，费城半导体指数屡创新高，市场对AI资本开支的乐观预期成为行情主引擎。但10月初以来，韩国这一高杠杆市场率先回调，叠加中国存储厂商长鑫存储（CXMT）在新芯片架构上取得进展、美国9月通胀超预期推高年内加息概率、10年期美债收益率逼近5%的多重压力，最终演变为本周全球芯片股的集中抛售，费城半导体指数较10月初高点已下跌12%。
key_points: 抛售从韩国蔓延：SK海力士和三星占KOSPI市值一半以上，本周二因估值过高担忧率先下跌，抛压迅速传导至日本和美国市场。
中国变量成导火索：长鑫存储宣布在更高密度芯片架构上取得进展，引发市场担心中国存储厂商正快速追赶国际巨头，加剧恐慌性卖出。
通胀与利率压制：美国9月CPI同比3.7%高于预期，PPI同比涨6.3%创2022年以来最快，市场押注美联储年内还将加息，10年期美债收益率一度触及5.34%。
AI支出回报存疑：Anthropic三季度营收168亿美元被解读为增速明显放缓，而超大规模云厂商今年资本开支约8000亿美元，市场担心投入产出不成正比。
融资成本飙升：CoreWeave 2032年到期债券收益率从发行时的9.625%飙至近15%，显示AI基建的借贷成本正在急剧上升。
摩根大通认为可能临近拐点：芯片股仍比6月历史高点低约15%，SK海力士与三星的财报显示主题性需求仍在，板块有望翻越这堵担忧之墙。
report.impact: 对AI行业，这轮调整意味着算力叙事开始被盈利与现金流检验，融资成本上升可能延缓部分数据中心扩张计划；对开发者，短期云算力价格与厂商补贴策略或有波动，但模型迭代不会停滞，推理效率优化价值更高；对普通用户，AI产品的低价红利可能收窄，但泡沫挤出后行业会更健康。
report.tools: 想跟进可盯住费城半导体指数（SOX）与10年期美债收益率两个风向标，跟踪SK海力士、三星、美光的HBM财报进展；开源侧可关注vLLM、SGLang等推理加速框架和Qwen、Llama系列模型，在算力涨价周期里压缩推理成本；云上可用CoreWeave、Lambda等GPU租赁平台做比价。
